source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Resting on fairly little established clinical rationale despite being routine practice for suspected bacteremia","B":"A single set generally being considered sufficient on its own, regardless of how strong the clinical suspicion happens to be","C":"A single set generally being considered to provide adequate diagnostic information in most clinical situations","D":"Two sets improve diagnostic sensitivity and help distinguish true bacteremia from contamination (which typically grows in only one set)"}}
source_row.rationale: Obtaining two sets of blood cultures from separate sites improves diagnostic sensitivity for detecting true bacteremia and helps distinguish true infection (which typically grows in multiple sets) from contamination (which typically grows in only one set).
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for Multiple Blood Culture Sets
source_row.source_name: Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute — Blood Culture Collection Guidelines
